** *
 NIDHI GUPTA, J.
CM-21044-CII-2025
Prayer in this application filed under Section 151 CPC is for condonation of delay of 56 days in refiling the accompanying appeal.

2. Heard.
3.
For the reasons mentioned in the application which is duly supported by an affidavit of the applicant/appellant No.1, the same is allowed and delay of 56 days in refiling the appeal is condoned.
Prayer in this application filed under Section 5 of the Limitation Act is for condonation of delay of 635 days in filing the appeal.

2. The only reason cited by the applicant/appellants in the above application for condonation of 635 days delay in filing the appeal is as under:-
FAO-5947-2025 (O&M) - 2- "1. That the Appellants is filing the instant appeal which is most likely to be allowed, otherwise in this case Appellants could not file the appeal with in time due to the reason that Appellants was not having the legal fees in this case and due to insufficient funds for legal fees and Appellants could arrange the same in the month of July, 2025 being amount of compensation was released in the month of march 2025, copy of voucher dt. 31.3.2025 is attached as Annexure A-1, rather actual payment was made in the month of July 2025, and after engaging the counsel on 8.7.2025 the same was prepared on 8.7.2025 and the same was filed on 9.7.2025 otherwise delay of 635 days in filing the appeal is not intentional but due to the reason mentioned above which was beyond the control of the Appellants."

sentences.text: The said reason is vague and does not constitute sufficient cause to condone extraordinary delay of 635 days in filing the present appeal.
Applicant has failed to specify as to how much fees was paid to legal counsel.
Applicant has also failed to specify as to what occasioned the delay in disbursement of compensation granted vide the Award dated 15.7.2023.

Furthermore, a perusal of the Pay Order dated 31.3.2025 (Annexure A-1) shows that vide the said Pay Order, an amount of Rs.4,45,826/-
only has been disbursed to the applicant/appellants out of total compensation of Rs.16,45,000/-.
There is no detail provided by the applicant as to when, and in what manner was the remaining amount of compensation disbursed to them.

The averments made in the application are, therefore,
vague and general.
It is cardinal principle of law that delay of each day has to be explained.

In this regard, reference may be made to a recent judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Civil Appeal No. 11794 of 2025 titled as Shivamma (Dead) by LRs Vs. Karnataka Housing Board and others, 2025 INSC 1104 decided on 12.09.2025, Law Finder Doc Id # 2777666, wherein it is held that each day's delay has to be explained in a mathematical manner which has not been done by the applicant-appellants.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: No cogent reason or plausible explanation has been furnished by the applicants for condonation of such an inordinate and unexplained delay in filing the accompanying appeal.
Moreover, condonation of such an inordinate delay would be tantamount to declaring the law of limitation obsolete/redundant, without any justification.
5. As such, no ground is made out for condoning inordinate delay of 635 days.
Present application accordingly stands dismissed.
The present appeal has been filed by the claimants seeking enhancement of compensation of Rs.16,45,000/- awarded by the ld.
Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Rohtak (hereinafter "the learned Tribunal") vide Award dated 15.07.2023 passed in MACP Case No. 380 dated 12.12.2019 filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act,
(hereinafter "the Act")
. The 5 claimants before the Tribunal are the widow; 2 children and parents of the deceased Deepak, who was 41 years old at the time of accident.
Present appeal has been filed by the widow; 19-year-old daughter; 16-year- FAO-5947-2025 (O&M) - 4- old son; and LRs of Father Krishan (now deceased).
Mother of the deceased is impleaded as performa respondent No.5 herein.

2. Brief facts of the case are that the ld. Tribunal on the basis of pleadings and evidence adduced before it concluded that the deceased- Deepak had died due to the injuries suffered by him in a motor vehicular accident that took place on 11.10.2019 due to the rash and negligent driving of a Truck bearing registration No. HR-46E/5781 (hereinafter "the offending vehicle") being driven by respondent No.1; owned by respondent No.2; and insured by respondent No.3.
The Tribunal awarded above said compensation along with interest @ 6% per annum.
Respondents No.1 to 3 were held liable to pay compensation jointly and severally.
3. The learned counsel for the appellants seeks enhancement of compensation by submitting that income of the deceased has been taken on the lower side as only Rs.10,000/- per month.

It is Jyoti And Others vs Kanwar Pal And Others on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26706836/
2 submitted that appellants have proved that deceased was working as a Driver.

sentences.text:
It is contended that even as per Minimum Wage Notification issued by the State of Haryana applicable w.e.f 01.01.2019 to 30.06.2019, minimum wage payable to a driver of light vehicle was Rs.412.68 per day i.e.
Rs.12,380.40 per month.
Copy of the said Notification is handed over in Court today which is taken on record.

4. Learned counsel further submits that interest has been awarded at meagre rate of 6% per annum;
whereas per judgment of Coordinate Bench of this Court passed in FAO-4023-2006 titled as 'Sushila and others vs. Bhagat Singh and others', decided on 17.01.2025, Neutral FAO-5947-2025 (O&M) - 5- Citation No. 2025:PHHC:007009, interest ought to have been awarded @ 18% per annum.

entities.text: Sushila and others vs. Bhagat Singh and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It has further been submitted that multiplier has not been correctly applied; deduction should be 1/5th; and future prospects ought to have been awarded @ 50%.
5.
It is accordingly prayed that present Appeal be allowed; and the compensation be enhanced in the above manner.
6. No other argument is raised on behalf of the appellants.
I have heard ld. Counsel and perused the case file in detail.
I find no merit whatsoever in the submissions made on behalf of the appellants.

7. Perusal of the record of the case shows that it was the pleaded case of the appellants that prior to the accident, deceased was working as a Driver and was also doing part time job at ration depot and thereby earning total amount of Rs.32,000/- per month.

To prove the above said assertion,
appellants had examined PW3 Devender, Depot Holder who had tendered his Affidavit Ex.PW3/A and who had deposed that deceased Deepak was working in his depot from 3:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m.
and was getting Rs.9,000/- per month as salary.

It is however to be noted that PW3 has admitted in his cross-examination that he had no certificate showing that he is a Depot Holder; and he even does 'not have any account Statement of my alleged Depot.'
PW3 has also admitted that he has no documentary proof of any employee working for him; including no documentary proof of the said alleged part-time employment of the deceased.
Thus, by no stretch of the imagination, can it be said that it was FAO-5947-2025 (O&M) - 6- proved that the deceased was in part-time employment and earning Rs.9,000/- per month.
8. As regards assertion of the appellants that deceased was working as driver, the appellants adduced no reliable evidence even in respect of these said employment.
Rather PW4 Rajni has admitted that she did not know registration number of the auto-rickshaw being allegedly driven by the deceased.
PW4 has also admitted that she did not know who was owner of the said auto-rickshaw.

In these circumstances, in the absence of any reliable evidence, Tribunal had correctly assessed income of the deceased as Rs.10,000/- p.m.
9.
Further the age of the deceased was determined to be 41 years at the time of accident on the basis of his PAN Card Ex.P11, wherein his date of birth is recorded as 06.06.1978.
Accordingly, learned Tribunal had correctly made addition of 25% towards future prospects; and had correctly applied multiplier of 14.
As there were 5 claimants, learned Tribunal had correctly made deduction of 1/4th towards personal expenses of the deceased.

Learned Tribunal had awarded an amount of Jyoti And Others vs Kanwar Pal And Others on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26706836/
3 Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate; Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses; and Rs.40,000/- towards loss of consortium to claimant No.1/widow; thereby granting total compensation of Rs.16,45,000/-
alongwith interest @ 6% per annum.
10.

sentences.text: Contention of the appellants that interest ought to have been awarded @ 18% per annum in terms of judgment passed in Sushila case (supra), is liable to be rejected as there is no hard and fast rule laid down FAO-5947-2025 (O&M) - 7- by the Hon'ble Supreme Court for grant of interest.
It is trite law that grant of interest is not a matter of right and entitlement.
Grant of the interest is at the discretion of the Court.
Moreover, even in said case of Sushila (supra), Coordinate Bench has granted interest @ 9% per annum.
Thus, no ground is made out for enhancement of interest as granted by learned Tribunal.
11. It is also to be seen that no prayer for grant of consortium has been made by the appellants either at the time of argument or in the present Grounds of Appeal.
As such, this Court cannot grant more than what is prayed for.
12. In view of above, the present appeal is dismissed on grounds of delay as well as on merits.
13. Pending application(s) if any also stand(s) disposed of.
Divyanshi JUDGE
